answer: Because the raven index resolves every citation against the ferrous checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the ivory audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 228 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 228 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 18 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
